How it is put together

Norilsk has three generators, three effect slots and a master delay and plate reverb. I think of the generators as furnaces: each one burns a sound. The effect slots are the pipes the sound goes through, and the delay and reverb are the air the fumes end up in. In practice:

  • Each generator plays through its own lane of effects: generator 1 through lane 1, 2 through 2, 3 through 3. A small part of each generator also goes straight to the master, dry.
  • Each lane is a chain of two or three effects, drawn from a recipe. An effect before the last one can also send to the master on its own.
  • The white keys play the generator you chose last, in the current scale. There are four voices, shared by the three generators.
  • Each generator has a level, pan, mute, delay and reverb sends, a looper and a DISINTEGRATOR. Each effect slot has a level, pan and mute.
  • One generator can modulate another (ring, amplitude or filter), but only if you link them by hand: hold SHIFT, hold one generator's button, then the other's.

The first processor core renders the voices. The second runs the effects and the master delay and reverb, one block (0.73 ms) behind.

Every sound swells in and keeps moving. However, nothing sounds on once no note is held, latched or looped: released voices fade out within three seconds, and the effect slots close two seconds after the last voice. The master delay and reverb are the exception: their tails always ring out in full, whatever you let go or mute.

What is random and what isn't

Almost nothing in Norilsk is set by hand at the start. It is drawn at random, and your job is to choose, keep, throw again and play. Randomness works at every scale:

  1. The sound. FURNACE, the engine, draws a sound from a family, a seed, a path and an engine generation. The same four values always give exactly the same sound, so a session only needs to store the seed.
  2. The note while it sounds. An invisible hand (after Anima) keeps moving the four macros of every voice. Russolo's grit drops bits, crosses the sound with itself and makes it stutter. The grains are read from places that wander. In other words, the same key held twice never sounds the same twice.
  3. A generator (HOME on a generator): a scene, a family chosen by how harsh it is allowed to be, which effects it is cabled into, and how much of it is heard dry.
  4. An effect slot (HOME on an effect slot): one of 24 recipes. Each place in the recipe is filled with one of its allowed effects that fits the slot's memory, every value is drawn around its default, and the outs are drawn too. HOME on a generator also draws its lane's chain.
  5. The paths. ABRASIVE and DARK bias every draw above: scenes, families, recipes and effect values.
  6. Partial draws. REWIRE draws only the cables. RAND PARAMS draws only an effect slot's values, or a new sound of the same family for a generator. SHIFT + HOME keeps the family or the recipe. Holding HOME draws all six slots.
  7. Modulation. SHIFT + SEQ draws a slot's two LFOs and two to six of its eight routes. The STEPS and DRIFT shapes and the RANDOM source keep drawing new values as they play.
  8. Playing. The DISINTEGRATOR gates, stutters, crushes and pans each generator in pulses of random length. The looper's VARY changes every note it plays, and RANDOM jumps between loops.
  9. What isn't random. A snapshot stores the whole machine and recalls it exactly, or morphs into it. Sessions keep everything in flash.

The black keys are contextual. A key that has no job in the current view does nothing there and stays dark.

The screen

The screen is designed for low vision: few words, very large type, high contrast.

The main view is drawn as a place. At the top there is slowly drifting smog, with the audio load on the left and the battery on the right. Below ground, the three effect slots are rusty pipes, one above the other. Each effect is a section between bolted flanges with its name on a dark plate: FLT filter, FLD fold, MU mulaw, SHF shift, MDL modal, STR string, VOX vowel, TAP tape, RVS reverse, SPR spring, GLT glitch, CLD cloud, SCR scream, RNG ring, STV starve, CHB cheb, BNK bank, SMR smear, DIF diffuse, SLW slew, XOR xor, DST dust.

Under each name there is a band in the colours of the generators feeding it. Plates fed by the chosen generator are filled with its colour. A section glows hotter while sound passes through it, and a muted pipe is cold grey.

At the bottom, the three generators are brick furnaces with fire in their mouths in their colours (red, blue, green). The fire is brighter while they sound and dark when they are muted. The chosen slot has a white frame. Cables are not drawn. KNOB 1 shows its value on a dial that covers the whole screen.

The generators

Each generator runs an instance of FURNACE, the engine, playing one sound drawn from thirty-six families. The four voices are shared by the three generators, and each voice is a complete instance of the engine. Because of this, the same sound on two keys never sounds quite the same. The engine is described in detail in FURNACE: the engine below.

The DISINTEGRATOR

KNOB 1 while playing sets the DISINTEGRATOR of the generator the keys play, 0 to 100. It is an unstable gate placed after the sound is made and before its cables, so the effects hear it too.

It cuts the sound into pulses of uneven length. Each pulse either lets the sound through, gates it down (to silence from 60 upwards), repeats a 10 to 90 ms slice of what was just played, or crushes it (bits and sample rate). A pulse may also throw the dry part across the stereo image.

The higher the value, the shorter and more irregular the pulses, and the more of them act, more deeply and more widely. Every edge is smoothed over about 1.5 ms, so there are no clicks. At 0 nothing is touched. Each generator keeps its own value in snapshots and sessions.

The ideas come from Destroy FX's Skidder and from buffer repeaters. None of their code is used.

FURNACE: the engine

FURNACE is the engine in each generator. It started as Tonitor's FM engine and was rebuilt around one goal: a sound that is never struck, never still and never exactly the same twice.

It works on one voice, one note and one block of 32 samples (0.73 ms at 44.1 kHz) at a time. Everything is integer maths, because the chip has no floating point, and the per-sample code runs from RAM. The code is in firmware/src/mol.c (the voice and the draw), fm6_core.c (the operators), wt.c (the waves) and found_clips.h (the found sounds).

A voice, stage by stage

Every block goes through these stages in this order:

  1. The hand (generation 3). An invisible hand rests on each voice (after Anima: Tonitor's version, from Vascular). One finger drags figures across a surface: orbits, figures of eight, scribbles, slow glides and the occasional flick. It presses in slow swells and sometimes lifts to land somewhere else, and a second "ghost" finger comes and goes. The fingers' position, pressure, speed, angle, distance and age are read once a block. Two to four of them, chosen when the sound is drawn, are mapped onto the sound's brightness, cloud, level, grit, glitches and cloud darkness. The hand never touches pitch.
  2. The operators. Six-operator FM: msfa (Dexed's core) in Felucca's integer port, as Tonitor shaped it. That means the DX7's 32 algorithms, four-rate / four-level envelopes, keyboard scaling, ratio or fixed frequencies, feedback and an LFO. Each operator reads a sine or one of 28 band-limited single cycles (four primitives, Bigorna's sixteen harmonic sets and eight made for bells). The wave can be morphed towards the next one in its bank, and its phase can be bent as on the Casio CZ, so a sine opens like a filter and a square's width follows its envelope. Each wave has eight levels of detail, and one is picked every block from the operator's frequency, so the wave itself never aliases. The macros act here: BRIGHTNESS on the modulators' index, DETUNE (or INHARMONIC) on the ratios, MOTION on the LFO and a tremolo. Finally a 7 Hz high-pass removes the DC that FM produces, and the sound's measured gain is applied.
  3. The exciter and the body (generation 4). The operators' sound, or noise, or a bow, drives a body tuned to the note. A TUBE is a waveguide: a delay line one period long, damped and low-passed inside its loop, with an allpass that adds a wire's stiffness (the partials are pulled apart). It can be open, or closed at one end, which leaves only odd partials. A MODAL body is six resonators tuned to the ratios of a bar, a plate, a bell, a closed pipe or a hull, slightly detuned. The bow is Smith's bowed string model: friction that grips while the string moves with the bow and slips when it doesn't. A body rings for 2.5 s at most and never bends the pitch.
  4. The grit (generation 3). Russolo's grit, after Robert Heel's Noisferatu. It has three parts: a small DAC (bits dropped, each sample held several times), XOR of the sample with a triangle at a ratio of the note (logic oscillators), and stutters, which loop the last 5 to 120 ms of the sound 3 to 12 times and then carry on. The grit is mixed with the clean sound, and the hand moves both the mix and the chance of a stutter.
  5. The grains. All of the above is written continuously into the voice's own buffer: 12288 samples at 22.05 kHz in 8-bit mu-law, about 0.56 s. Up to four grains at once read it back, in one of two ways. A CLOUD plays grains of 2 to 400 ms at its own rate (1 to 400 per second), starting at a drifting point behind the write head. The grains are jittered in time and level, pitched by the sound's intervals, sometimes reversed, darkened by a low-pass and fed back into the buffer, so the cloud smears on itself. When the sound asks for it, the cloud is FROZEN: the buffer stops recording a moment after the note starts, and the cloud keeps turning over what it holds. PULSARS (after Curtis Roads) are grains locked to the note's period, from half a grain to four grains per period. One grain per period reads the sound back as a formant, and a burst mask drops some grains, which adds a sub-harmonic. From generation 5, a share of the grains reads a found sound instead (see below). The GRAIN macro changes the cloud's share and rate, and gives a sound without a cloud the cloud drawn with it.
  6. The hand's pressure on the level, last.

A voice ends when its note has been released and it has been silent for a quarter of a second, or when its operators, body and cloud have nothing left to play. Separately, the generators fade a released voice out within three seconds.

The found sounds (generation 5)

There are sixteen clips of 0.6 s in flash, stored in 8 bits like the grain buffers, each looping without a seam:

  • Ice and the sea, from NOAA's hydrophones: an iceberg calving, its tremor, an icequake, a grounding, and a ship above the Challenger Deep.
  • The aurora's radio emissions, from NASA's Polar spacecraft: auroral hiss (twice), kilometric radiation, chorus and "saucers".
  • A plant, rendered here: a transformer, an air duct, a furnace, rain on tin, an engine room and wind in wires.

A grain can start anywhere in its clip. Its playback rate follows the keys only by a drawn share, so the clip is barely transposed. DEPTHS, AURORA and PLANT take 70 to 100 % of their grains from a clip. Older sounds with a cloud get a clip one time in three, for 30 to 60 % of their grains. Sources and credits are in found/CREDITS.md.

How a sound is drawn

A sound is drawn from four values: a family, a seed, a path and a generation. The same four values always give the same sound, bit for bit. This is why a session stores the seed and not the sound itself. The draw goes like this:

  1. Family. Chosen from the generator's scene and a harshness budget (HOME), or kept (SHIFT + HOME). The scene also sets the draw's path: FIELD uses the ambient path, MATERIAL the open one, FEEDBACK and EROSION the experimental one.
  2. Body. One of eight FM bodies. The newer families each borrow one and build on it.
  3. The family's own features: a cloud, shattered grains, pulsars, a freeze, grit and logic, an exciter and body, or a found sound.
  4. The path. AMBIENT makes the sound slower and darker: longer attacks and releases, lower modulators, a longer cloud, and one time in three an octave down. EXPERIMENTAL makes it harsher: modulators and feedback up, mutated more often than not. On the open path one sound in three is mutated. A mutation fixes a partial to a frequency, turns an envelope upside down, pushes the feedback, moves an octave, replaces a sine with another wave, or bends one.
  5. Care. Modulators on high ratios are turned down, the index is scaled down the keyboard, and the carriers get rate scaling.
  6. Generation 2's rule. Every sound swells in, holds and keeps moving: a slow LFO (0.1 to 1 Hz) on the modulators' levels, no pitch envelope, and a cloud that fades in.
  7. Later generations. Most sounds (85 %) get the hand. Some older families get grit on the experimental path. One older sound in five gets a body, and one older cloud in three gets a found sound.
  8. Sanitiser. Every value is forced into its range.
  9. Measurement. The sound is rendered for 2.5 s at middle C, outside the audio path, and its loudest 46 ms are brought to a fixed level. The boost is limited to +15.6 dB, so a slow swell stays a swell.

The generations

A sound keeps the generation it was drawn under, and a generation never changes what it draws. The tests check this with a hash of hundreds of sounds for each generation. In practical terms, a session from an older build sounds exactly as it did. New sounds are always drawn on the newest generation.

GenerationWhat it added
0FM with waves in the operators, the grains, twelve families
1No pitch bends in the bodies (no zaps, no bleeps), the tonal ones roughened; no freeze before the body has sounded
2Textures and drones only: IMPACT and PULSE are no longer drawn; every sound swells in, holds and keeps moving
3The hand, the grit, eight families
4The exciter and the body, five families
5The found sounds, three families
6Eight families; one older sound in four gets other waves (harmonic sets, bells, bent)

The macros

There are four macros on the EDIT page, each from -64 to 64. At 0 you hear the sound exactly as drawn. The response is the square root of the knob's travel, so the first part of the turn has the most effect.

  • BRIGHTNESS moves the modulators' index about 27 dB either way, tilts the higher carriers up and raises the feedback with it.
  • DETUNE pulls the carriers apart (up to 40 cents) and moves the modulators off their carriers. On metallic and noisy bodies it becomes INHARMONIC, which moves every operator except the lowest carrier off its ratio.
  • GRAIN makes the cloud wetter and faster, or drier and slower. On a sound without a cloud, it fades in the cloud drawn with that sound.
  • MOTION sets the LFO's depths, adds a tremolo (1.5 to 6 Hz) and moves the grains' drift.

The hand, the LFOs (SEQ) and you can all move the macros at the same time.

The effect slots

There are twenty-two effects, two or three to a slot. The last five were added in build 32, and their names are provisional. The delay and plate reverb belong to the master only (since build 30). If a session was saved with them in a slot, they load as TAPE and SPRING.

EffectWhat it is
FILTERA driven state-variable filter: low-pass, band-pass, high-pass or notch. Resonant up to the edge of screaming, never piercing
FOLDA wavefolder, with a second fold and a tone control
MULAWRate and bit reduction, with the filter open enough to alias and a drive into it
SHIFTA frequency shifter: every partial moved by the same 40 to 900 Hz, which tears the harmony apart
MODALThree tuned resonators, spread inharmonically, ringing up to Q 325
STRINGThree Karplus-Strong strings on the scale's root, ringing up to 8 s
VOWELThree formants morphing through the vowels, driven
TAPEAn echo through a worn head: dropouts, saturation, age, hiss under the sound
REVERSEWindows of the sound played backwards, fed back
SPRINGA spring tank, with its chirps
GLITCHRussolo's bent buffers: jumps and stutters through the last 0.74 s, never at another pitch
CLOUDA granular cloud that can freeze what it holds
SCREAMA shaped feedback howl
RINGA diode ring modulator that modulates itself
STARVEA starved, gated fuzz (after the Fuzz Factory)
CHEBA harmonic re-voicer using Chebyshev polynomials (after Airwindows' Pafnuty)
BANKAn inharmonic resonator bank: a bar, a plate, a bell, a membrane (after Mutable Instruments' Rings)
SMEARThe sound through twenty random taps, each + or −, over 12 to 46 ms: a grainy haze rather than a room (a velvet-noise decorrelator)
DIFFUSEFour allpasses in series (with the lengths from Mutable Instruments' Clouds): blurred edges, no tail of its own
SLEWLimits how far the sound can move in one sample, turning the highs into dark, grinding ramps (after Airwindows' Slew)
XORThe sound combined bit by bit (XOR, AND, OR) with itself a moment earlier: broken and digital, but following its shape
DUSTHiss and crackle where the sound moves, none where it is still (after Airwindows' TapeDust)

Twenty-four recipes decide which effects may stand at each place: SPACE, ECHO, METAL, STRINGS, EROSION, GHOST, SPECTRAL, RESONANT, FOLDS, TELEPHONE, HELL, FACTORY, GLITCH, BROADCAST, ABYSS, RUST, FREEZER, FEEDBACK, FOUNDRY, GONG, SPECTRE, SPUTTER, SMOG, STATIC.

Every effect falls silent when nothing comes in. None of them sounds on by itself.

The lanes

Generator 1 plays through lane 1 only, generator 2 through lane 2, generator 3 through lane 3. Each generator is cabled into the head of its lane, with a small dry share. There are no cables between lanes. The lanes sit centre, left and right.

HOME on a generator also draws its lane's chain, so the chain is part of the generator's patch (SHIFT + HOME keeps the family and the recipe). HOME on an effect slot draws that lane again and keeps its generator. REWIRE inside a lane redraws where the generator enters and which effects also send to the master. Holding HOME draws all three generators and their lanes.

From build 28 to 35 a session could also be MESH: any generator cabled into any effect, and effects cabled across slots. In practice it mostly produced smear, so from build 36 there are only lanes. A MESH session loads rewired into lanes, snapshots included, with nothing redrawn.

The paths

Two black keys bias everything HOME draws, and RAND PARAMS too:

  • ABRASIVE (2nd black key): gnarly, textural, torn. It favours the experimental scenes; the harsh families (BRUIT, SHATTER, FURNACE, STATIC, SCRAPE, DATA, METAL); more cables and cross-modulation; the torn and crushed recipes; and higher drive, breakage and crushing in the effects.
  • DARK (3rd black key): dark ambient, drones, introspection, along the lines of Lustmord and the Cold Meat Industry catalogue. It favours the FIELD scene; drones, hums, tunnels, ash and freezes, nothing harsh; the spacious and ringing recipes (SPACE, GHOST, ABYSS, FREEZER, RESONANT, GONG and others); and darker, less driven values with larger spaces. It is also 3 dB quieter.

With neither on, anything goes. The path is saved with the session and with each snapshot.

Modulation

Every slot, generator or effect slot, has two LFOs and eight routes, A to H.

  • The LFO shapes are SINE, TRI, SAW UP, SAW DOWN, SQUARE, STEPS and DRIFT. Each LFO runs FREE, restarts on each NOTE, or runs ONCE, and has a fade-in.
  • A route goes from a source (LFO 1, LFO 2, VELOCITY, KEY, RANDOM) to a destination, by an amount.
  • A generator's destinations are its four macros, level, pan, sends and the LFOs' rates.
  • An effect slot's destinations are the values of its effects by place, its level, pan and the LFOs' rates. Because routes point at a place and not at an effect, after HOME draws new effects the LFO moves the new effect's value at that place.

SEQ's third page sets them, and SHIFT + SEQ draws them at random.

Snapshots and sessions

A snapshot is the whole machine. It stores every slot's sound, effects, values and cables; levels, pans, mutes and sends; the DISINTEGRATORs; the FX MIX; the master delay and reverb; the modulation; the scale and root; the octave; and the path. It also stores how the machine is being played: the latched notes, whether each generator's loops are playing, which loops are taken out, their direction and speed, VARY, and moves along the scale. The loop recordings themselves belong to the session. There are sixteen snapshots in a session.

SAVE opens the SNAPSHOTS page. Release a white key to recall its snapshot. Hold it 0.8 s to store the current state in it. Hold SHIFT as well to empty it.

KNOB 1 on this page sets the morph time, 0 to 30 s. A recalled snapshot moves into place over that time. Levels, pans, sends, values and LFOs glide. Sounds cross-fade on voices of their own, and effect chains are faded out and in, one after the other. Anything that has no in-between value switches halfway through. The square and key of the target snapshot blink until the morph is finished.

SHIFT + SAVE opens the SESSIONS list, as on Bigorna: four to a page, and PRESETS moves through the 64 slots. A saved session is white, an empty slot grey, and the loaded one is marked on its right. SAVE opens that slot's page:

  • BACK
  • LOAD, or NEW on an empty slot (a clean slate)
  • SAVE (asks first if it would overwrite another session)
  • COPY to a slot chosen with PRESETS. The first empty slot is offered; copying over a session asks first
  • DELETE (asks first)

PRESETS moves through the rows, SAVE runs the selected one, and SHIFT + SAVE goes back a level. While playing, holding SAVE saves straight into the loaded session. A session holds the machine, its sixteen snapshots, the latched notes and every loop, in the FM-1's flash.

Norilsk only writes to blank flash or to its own retired sessions, never over another firmware's data. However, other firmware does not return the favour, so back up your sessions before installing something else.

The looper

Each generator has Tonitor's looper: up to ten free-running loops, each on its own clock. There is no tempo and no grid.

Press REC to arm a loop; the first note starts it. Press REC again to end it, and it plays at once. Press REC again while the loops play to overdub. A note held across the end of a loop is tied over.

Holding PLAY shows the loops on the white keys, so you can take them out or bring them back. It also lights the 4th to 8th black keys: REVERSE, PENDULUM, RANDOM, HALF SPEED, DOUBLE SPEED. SHIFT + OCT moves every loop along the scale, and SHIFT + REC turns on VARY.

Backing up sessions

The website's backup page saves every session on the FM-1 to a file and writes them back, from desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera.

From a terminal, tools/fm1_sessions.py lists the sessions, tools/fm1_sessions.py save N saves one and tools/fm1_sessions.py restore FILE writes one back. Both the page and the script only talk to an FM-1 whose USB name is FM-1 Norilsk.

USB audio

Connected to a computer, the FM-1 is also a class-compliant USB audio interface, so no driver is needed. It sends the stereo master at 16 bits, 48 kHz (or 44.1 kHz), taken before the MASTER knob. This means a recording does not follow the headphone level. The code comes from Tonitor and Bigorna.

Developed by Nuno Zimas. Firmware: GPL-3.0. Website and logo: MIT. Source on GitHub.

M-VAVE and FM-1 are trademarks of their owner, used only to say which device Norilsk runs on. Norilsk is named after the city; it has nothing to do with the company that runs its smelters.
